title: Sonia Exelby: Man on trial in killing of woman he met on porn site Motherless | CNN
text:
EDITOR’S NOTE:Warning: This story contains graphic descriptions of violence and references to self-harm and suicide.

Source: CNN

A Florida man is on trial accused of kidnapping and killing a British woman last year after meeting her on the now defunct Motherless.com, an extreme porn site that has drawn international scrutiny forhosting graphic sexual abuseand other content depicting gender-based violence.

Prosecutors in Marion County, Florida, argue that Dwain Hall, 54, killed Sonia Exelby, a 32-year-old music tutor from southern England in October 2025 after grooming her on the site for roughly two years before she traveled to the United States.Hall has pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder and kidnapping.

Exelby had a history of mental illness, according to her family, and had struggled with severe depression and suicidal ideation, having tried twice to take her own life, the court heard.

In her opening statement, Florida assistant state attorney Amy Berndt said that Exelby “was always trying to find some substitute” for self-harming, and that a group of men she found onMotherlesshad provided an outlet for her.

“Sonia was communicating on Motherless with many different men. She was trying to find somebody that would kill her. Her mental health was declining. She wanted to die, and she knew that she couldn’t do it herself,” Berndt said.

“Unfortunately, there was no shortage of depraved men willing to kill Sonia in the most torturous and vile ways possible. And they would send her messages and describe to her how they would kill her.”

Hall, who used the alias Alpha Sadist on the site, along with other usernames, preyed on that vulnerability to act out a “sadistic pleasure,” according to prosecutors.

They say he demanded Exelby pay $4,000 in cash to kill her.

Hall, who denies killing Exelby, told police that he had been intimate with her.

Hall’s defense team has said that he was trying to help a woman who wanted to die.

In October 2025, Exelby flew to the United States, where Hall picked her up from Florida’s Gainesville Regional Airport. From there, prosecutors say, he drove her to an Airbnb.

Prosecutors showed a text message to the court that Exelby had allegedly sent to a friend during her time spent with Hall.

It read: “I’m sorry he keeps taking my phone he doesn’t trust me with it. He made it clear there was no way out unless I shoot him. … No one will find me in time … I thought he’d do it quick and not give my mind time to stew and (realize) this is the last thing I’ll ever (say) to anyone if I don’t take his offer of shooting him.”

Exelby’s body was found by police investigators on October 17, 2025, after Interpol contacted them about a woman reported missing to police in Britain.

Her body was recovered from a shallow grave, with four stab wounds and bruising.

Jurors this week were shown video recovered from Hall’s phone in which he ordered Exelby to repeat that she wanted to be beaten and suffer.

“This is how you wanted to die, right? You wanted to be beaten and made to suffer because you’re such a piece of sh*t? Say it,” Hall said in the video.

Prosectors have presented physical, digital and financial evidence linking Hall to Exelby’s death, including a purchased shovel and a knife that DNA testing showed had Exelby’s blood on it.

Investigators also found numerous images of other women being raped, tortured and murdered on Hall’s mobile phone, the court heard, including graphic and “horrific” photographs of sexual violence.

In court, Exelby’s sister Sara told jurors about Sonia’s difficult childhood and detailed her mental health struggles. But despite personal challenges, Sara said her sister was always supportive and kind.

“She felt she was a burden, which she absolutely wasn’t, but she just had such a beautiful nature,” Sara said.

The trial, which began on Tuesday, is expected to last at least a week.

The case has underscored concerns about the role that some online platforms continue to play in the abuse of women, known as technology-facilitated violence against women and girls.

Motherless, which was at the center of aCNN investigationinto onlinedrug-facilitated sexual assaultearlier this year, was taken offline in May by Dutch authorities.

And in July, US Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton won a victory in cutting off Motherless’ ability to operate under the .com registry.
